**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/FalkorDB/FalkorDB/compare/v4.22.1...v4.22.2

A short read — a diskless-replication stream dropping mid-transfer, a truncated RESTORE/MIGRATE payload, or a corrupt dump.rdb — previously panicked the server, or in release builds silently built a corrupt graph. FalkorDB now declares REDISMODULE_OPTIONS_HANDLE_IO_ERRORS and checks for truncation at every count and loop in the decoders, so RESTORE replies with an error and an RDB load or diskless sync is refused, with no crash and no leaked graph.

# FalkorDB 6.0.0
For applications nothing changes: it is still a Redis module named `graph`, with the same `GRAPH.*` commands, the same Cypher, and the same client libraries. What changes is how replication works and which pac
- Bump Redis to 8.10.2 for CVE-2026-85091. Updates the pinned Redis version across all Docker images (build + server) and the sanitizer/test paths. (#2850, fixes #2849)

* HeavyConnect exposes external data through foreign tables that you can analyze with HeavyDB simplifying ETL workflows. Supported adapters include CSV/delimited files, Parquet, and regex-parsed logs on local storage or Amazon S3. ODBC database connectivity and raster data sources.
This project now includes access to not only the core HeavyDB server, but also all the functionality of the full HeavyAI platform, previously only available as an enterprise product.

Performance: multi-hop `$relation` queries expand from their targets instead of checking every record of the label (2 hops on a 100K-node graph: minutes → milliseconds); filtered vector search is routed on the matching-record count and filters during the ANN walk; exact vector search, grouped aggregates and unindexed filters run in parallel parts with results independent of the thread count; a plain `select` runs as a listing; lower CSV ingest memory and write volume.
